title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0LE1LF_---1LA_1LA0LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0LE1LF_---1LA_1LA0LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the two sweeps over the (01) stretches and the situations that lead to a halt (kernel), and no halt in the first 107 steps (native_decide); the C simulator finds no halt in 109 steps.

What it does. At the left end the tape reads (01)k₁ 1 (01)k₂ 1 (01)k₃ …, a list of numbers k, most of them odd (3 is the most common), with rare defects such as 10100. At the right end the same list appears in the words 1110, 1101, 1011, 0111. The sweeps translate between the two forms; the numbers near the left end change irregularly from trip to trip (stretches merge and split), while the list further right is carried along almost unchanged.
Where a halt would come from. Only E reading a 0 halts; E is entered from D reading a 0, so 0 D>0 halts. In 2·108 steps E always reads a 1.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 49,957 cells have been visited and 31,597 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: Going right, B turns each 1010 into 1101 (four steps a copy); going left, D with a 1 ahead turns each 1101 into 0101 (six steps a copy).

claims.title: The halting situations
claims.text: 0 D>0 halts after one step, 0 0 A>1 after two, 0 C>1 1 after three.

claims.title: E never reads a 0 in 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps
claims.text: In the first 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps the machine is in state E 17,398,306 times, every time on a 1: the halting transition E0 is never close to firing in a way the run shows.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The list of numbers k changes at its left end in a way nobody has described; NGramCPS with n ≤ 10 leaves it open.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. At its left end this machine keeps a list of numbers, written as stretches of 0 1 0 1 between single 1s, and the numbers near the end change from trip to trip. This page runs it in your browser.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 49,957 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A list written in stretches of 01
html: Stop the simulator when the head reaches the left end. The tape reads like (01)25 1 (01)17 1 (01)35 1 (01)11 1 (01)3 …: a list of numbers, each stretch of 01s closed by a single 1. Most numbers are odd, and 3 is by far the most common.
Going right, B rewrites each 1010 as 1101, four steps a copy, so at the right end the list appears in the words 1110, 1101, 1011, 0111:
Going left, D (with a 1 ahead) turns each 1101 back into 0101, six steps a copy (Lean: right_B, left_D).
The far part of the list is carried along almost unchanged, but near the left end stretches merge and split from trip to trip. That part looks random.

sections.heading: E must read a 0
html: Only E reading a 0 halts; E is entered from D reading a 0 and moving left:
E is entered 17 million times in the first 2·108 steps, always on a 1.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.499). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.502).
After 109 steps the tape spans 49,957 cells (15,917 left of the start, 20,545 right), with a density of 1s of 0.632.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Two-sided bouncer: at the left end the tape is a list of stretches (01)<sup>k</sup>, k mostly odd, separated by single 1s; the stretches near the left end merge and split from trip to trip while the rest is carried along. Open.
family: list of (01)-stretches separated by single 1s, two-sided bouncer
